work_order.approach: Amend the criterion where the criterion was wrong, and change the mechanism where the code was wrong — two different fixes, not one patch. AC-4 is corrected to what docs/ui.md already says: remove/archive/leave (plus rotate/disable) keep their naming confirms, while rename keeps its direct save plus success note (T-5's flow); no rename component is touched. The silent double-claim is fixed by moving failure feedback out of the component the action's own revalidation unmounts: claimPlaceholder stops returning inline error state for the two shapes a stale join page can actually produce and redirects instead — seat-taken goes to /join/<token>?claim=taken, rendered as a panel-level alert above the (now empty) seat list with the plain join still offered, and already-a-member goes to the group page, consistent with the page-load member bounce. Malformed-input and invalid-token errors stay inline because they never re-render the list. Unit tests assert the redirects; the atomic UPDATE … WHERE user_id IS NULL plus 23505 coverage is untouched.
assumptions: Any signed-in member may add a placeholder by name; only the owner may rename, remove members, archive, rotate or disable the invite link.

Placeholder claim is open seat-pick stated once: a non-member claiming an unclaimed placeholder adopts that row (UPDATE ... WHERE user_id IS NULL) and that adoption IS the join; joining without claiming inserts a fresh member row; a user who already holds a membership row cannot claim another placeholder (rejected under unique (group_id, user_id)); double-claim is rejected atomically with the existing unique-violation pattern mapping 23505 to a user-safe error.
Group type is the closed TRD set trip/home/couple/other, NOT NULL defaulting to 'other' with the form pre-selected; currency reuses SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (INR default from profile).

Archive hides the group from the home list but members can still open it with a read-only banner; archived groups reject join/claim/mutation writes (leave still permitted); there is no unarchive in this ticket. Removal here means member-row delete, not group delete.
Owner leave or self-remove transfers ownership to the earliest-joined remaining member; the last member leaving archives the group.

Invite token is 32 bytes CSPRNG base64url stored unique; disable flips invite_enabled, rotate issues a fresh token and the old one stops working; token and enabled flag are re-checked at submit time, not just on page load.
work_order.confidence_rationale: BUG-2 resolves by evidence rather than judgment: ui.md destructive-actions list, T-5's passing flow, and the implementation all agree rename has no confirm, so amending AC-4 cannot break a passing test. BUG-1's mechanism is confirmed in code and matches QA's observed empty-seat silent refresh; redirect-with-message is the standard Next pattern for exactly this unmount hazard and is unit-assertable. Held below 90 because no live preview was available in this checkout (groups code lives on the PR branch) and the already-member-to-group-page redirect is a small behavior change beyond the reported bug.
work_order.debate_summary: The round-2 critique filed ten findings (2 blocking, 5 major, 3 minor) plus edge cases and regression risks, and after re-checking the evidence I adopted all ten rather than splitting the difference: (1) the join-then-claim contradiction is real — unique (group_id, user_id) makes a post-join claim a duplicate — so AC-3 is rewritten as claim-as-join with the policy stated once; (2) the round-1 rejection item 2 truly was not fixed and the v2 understanding sentence claiming it was is removed, with the negative matrix now actually listed in actions.test.ts; (3) groupScope validation is added; (4) sign-in/sign-up/auth-form join files[] with a validated same-origin next; (5) member ActivityEvent writers ship in 0003 with this slice per the issue parenthetical and the project invariant rather than being parked; (6) AC-4 keeps only the browser-observable half with the guard-seam proof moved to AC-7, and the 'leaves as sole flow' fragment is fixed; (7) rotation-failure retention is test-proven with the browser criterion kept to drivable states; (8) DB-backed claim cases move from members.test.ts to actions.test.ts; (9) the duplicate CSPRNG generator is unified behind one shared helper; (10) missing group type defaults to 'other'. Load-bearing edge cases folded in: owner-leave transfer, archived-group write guards, atomic claim with 23505 mapping, stale-token re-check, malformed-id 404. The remainder (placeholder-name duplicates policy, 200-member rendering, double-submit idempotency, token hygiene in logs) stays in residual risks. No finding was dismissed; the only correction to the critique is that its regression-risk evidence line rightly notes the v2 evidence omitted the scripts/neon-smoke.ts scan exemption, which this plan records.

work_order.root_cause: (1) Criterion defect behind T-10/BUG-2: the v1 AC-4 demanded an explicit naming confirm for rename, but docs/ui.md lists only delete-expense, delete-payment, remove-member, rotate/disable-invite and archive-group as confirm-gated, the suite's own passing T-5 drives rename as direct save plus success note, and RenameGroupForm has no ConfirmStep by design — the code was right and the criterion contradicted its own rule source, so no code change on rename can green the loop. (2) Code defect behind BUG-1: claim-failure feedback is stored as per-seat useActionState inside the ClaimSeatForm, while the action's blanket revalidatePath('/') refreshes the join page to zero seats and unmounts that exact form — the SEAT_TAKEN message the code sets is discarded with the component holding it, so the stale claimant sees a silent refresh. The v1 diagnosis proved state correctness (atomic UPDATE, 23505 mapping) but never message survivability.

work_order.understanding: The v1 work order was wrong about AC-4 and silent about the real BUG-1 mechanism. First, v1's AC-4 required an explicit naming confirm for rename alongside remove/archive/leave — but docs/ui.md gates only delete-expense, delete-payment, remove-member, rotate/disable-invite and archive-group behind confirms, the QA suite's own passing T-5 drives rename as fill plus Save name plus success note with no confirm step, and RenameGroupForm has no ConfirmStep by design. T-10 (fail) and T-5 (pass) cannot both be satisfied: adding a rename confirm to fix T-10 breaks T-5's save-then-note flow. So BUG-2/T-10 fails against the criterion's letter, not the code — the code was right, and AC-4 is amended here to exclude rename (kept at id AC-4, same position, per the root-cause agent's criterion-is-wrong rule) with the corrected expectation locked in as new AC-10. Second, BUG-1 is a genuine defect v1 never diagnosed: the losing double-claim IS rejected server-side (atomic UPDATE ... WHERE user_id IS NULL, correct), but the SEAT_TAKEN message is set on the per-seat ClaimSeatForm's useActionState while the action's blanket revalidatePath('/') refreshes the join page to zero seats, unmounting that very form — the intended rejection is never visible. The fix is therefore a different mechanism, not a re-roll: redirect-with-message (seat-taken to /join/<token>?claim=taken rendered at panel level, already-member to the group page) instead of in-place form state, covered by new AC-9. Third, the refused v2 draft in previous-output.json was right on both diagnoses and wrong only formally: it dropped source/verify from every acceptance criterion, so it neither answered nor deferred IAC-1, IAC-2, IAC-3. This revision keeps that substance unchanged and restores full sourcing — AC-1..AC-8 keep their v1 sources with AC-4's check amended in place, and new AC-9/AC-10 carry IAC-2/IAC-3 — with no criterion renumbered or dropped.

issue_snapshot.title: Groups and members with invite links and placeholders
issue_snapshot.body:
Friends can create a group, invite by link, claim placeholder seats and manage membership, establishing the authorization boundary.

Person sees: home group list with per-group balance slot, group detail header and settings shell, members-and-invite screen (member list with owner badges, invite panel with copy, disable and rotate, placeholder add-by-name, claim prompts). Contract: DEFINES the groups and memberships schema plus the membership-first authorization pattern every later group route copies: (sessionUser, groupScope, zod-validated input), 401 unauthenticated, 404 when missing or not a member, double-claim of a placeholder rejected. Constraints: TR-7 including non-zero-balance block and membership-scoped visibility; per-request Pool lifecycle applies to all new queries.

**Risk.** Authorization and boundary risk: server-side membership checks on every group read and write, indistinguishable 404s, unguessable invite tokens with disable and rotate, balance-blocked removal.

**Out of scope**
- Expense entry and split math
- Balances, simplification and payments
- Activity feed UI (expense and payment writers land with their own slices)

Covers: TR-3, TR-7, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #4.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Create a group with name, currency and type and see it listed; only members can open it and missing-or-forbidden reads are indistinguishable with no data leak
- **IAC-2** Share an owner invite link, join as a second user, claim a placeholder added by name, and rotate or disable the link with an explicit confirm naming the link
- **IAC-3** Rename, remove, archive and leave flows work with confirms; removal or leave with a non-zero balance is blocked with a message pointing at settle-up

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

review.detail:
AC-4 and the PR QA script require the rename flow to sit behind an explicit confirm naming the object, but RenameGroupForm saves on one click with no confirm step.

`components/groups-panels.tsx:196`

Evidence: git show origin/sdlc/issue-5:components/groups-panels.tsx | grep -n ConfirmStep shows confirm usages at lines 375, 388 (rotate/disable), 452 (remove), 485 (archive), 579 (leave) — none inside RenameGroupForm (lines 196-236), which renders only a Save name button. Work-order AC-4 check: 'Rename, remove-member, archive and leave flows each require an explicit confirm naming the object'. Counter-evidence: docs/ui.md destructive-actions pattern lists remove/rotate/disable/archive (not rename), so the code matches the spec while the AC text over-requires.

Fix: Either add a ConfirmStep naming the group to RenameGroupForm, or (more consistent with ui.md, where rename is not a destructive action) amend AC-4 and the QA script to require confirms only for remove/archive/leave/rotate/disable.
